The code snippet calls `tree.children().get(index)` multiple times within the `forwardPropagateTree` method. The API method `get` throws `IndexOutOfBoundsException` if the index is out of range (i.e., index < 0 or index >= size). In the snippet:
- In the branch `else if (tree.isPreTerminal())`, `tree.children().get(0)` is called without any prior check on the children list size. If the children list is empty, this will throw `IndexOutOfBoundsException`.
- In the branch `else if (tree.children().size() == 2)`, `tree.children().get(0)` and `tree.children().get(1)` are called after explicitly verifying that the size is 2, so indices 0 and 1 are guaranteed to be valid.
- Other branches do not call `get` on the children list.

Thus, the `IndexOutOfBoundsException` is only potentially thrown in the preTerminal branch if the children list is empty. There is no validation to avoid this condition.
